_comment: Build order for the L5R character sheet. recombine.py concatenates every
`file` below, in this order, and writes the single-file HTML the app has
always been. Nothing is transformed on the way through -- the output is
`lines` records where each fragment came from in the pre-split deliverable.
split.py uses it to carve the original up; recombine.py ignores it entirely.
It is kept as provenance, so any fragment can be traced back to the exact
lines of the build it was cut from.
Adding a source file means adding an entry here, in the position it should
occupy. Order in this list IS the build order.
The fragments under src/sheet/ are pieces of ONE IIFE, not modules. They are
concatenation units: no fragment parses as standalone JavaScript, and none
is meant to. Splitting the IIFE into real modules would mean changing the
sheet's logic, which this phase explicitly does not do.

PART I Feature 4.53 - Configuration repairs. Eleven confirmed defects in already-shipped Phase 4.5 code, corrected additively: three wrong catalogue values, two stated entry-price reductions that never applied, Friendly Kami's unenforced Shugenja requirement, Great Potential's missing attack contexts, permissive pick validation, silently dropped unknown configs, and effects resolved from the wrong list. Ordered LAST among the 4.5 fragments so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.52's rather than being wrapped by them. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.54 - Configuration UX pass. Adds a touch-reachable circled-i beside every explanatory title= on the configured surface, because title= does nothing without hover and all fourteen tenet rules were unreadable on a phone. Purely additive: the title= attributes stay, so desktop hover is unchanged, and the button carries no text node so row textContent assertions still hold. Also rewords 4.5.2's 'XP refund' step labels through its own steps() seam. Ordered after 209.89 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.53's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.55 - Eligibility gates and Great Potential's Skill picker. Greys out an ineligible entry in the quick-add pickers with the reason in its label (Friendly Kami, Elemental Imbalance), recomputed each recalc because the pickers are built once at load but eligibility depends on School. Takes its eligibility VERDICT from Feature 4.53 where 4.53 knows the entry, so the greyed option and the row explaining itself cannot disagree. Also replaces Great Potential's bare text field with a single-select list of the character's own Skills, School-granted ones first and badged, plus an 'Another Skill...' escape that reveals the validated text field for a Skill not yet bought. The cards drive the same #advConfigFreeText input 209.81 already commits from, so the commit path is untouched. Ordered after 209.9 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.54's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.56 - Perceived Honor (A10) and Wealthy (A16), two of the audit's 23 missing configuration handlers. Adds a free-number rankFreePick type on the ADVANTAGE side: Phase 4.5.2's D45.install() seam was tried first and refused, because D45.refresh() hard-codes that a d45 entry must sit in #disadvList. Perceived Honor prices 2 XP per rank and derives its perceived-Honor readout from f_honorRank without touching it; Wealthy prices rank x 1 XP with a single total discount for Crane/Unicorn/Imperial and records its koku as an entitlement reminder rather than minting money. Ordered after 209.91 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.55's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.5.13 - Blackmail, Forbidden Knowledge, Inheritance and Way of the Land: named choices, scoped XP calculation, manual reminders and revision validation through the existing modal/save system. No registry seat, dice changes or grants.

PART I Feature 4.5.14 - Darling of the Court (A04): every purchased court on one row, 2 XP each or 1 for a Courtier School, one selected court and one persisted Court-in-session toggle, contextual Status +1 readout that never writes Status. Servant (A11): reference-only row and source examples; no servant record or cost change. No registry seat, dice changes or grants. Ordered after 209.925 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.5.13's.

PART I Feature 4.5.15 - General per-roll declaration registry. Entries register a provider (what it offers for a roll context, what an armed option does); this fragment owns the preview checkboxes, the transient state bound to the one roll context the preview opened with, the reset on open and cancel, and the route to the dice through the existing adv-config seat by wrapping advConfigExtendedRollModifiers. Damage is excluded centrally. Four delimited hooks in Phase 3's (Part G) 208-feat-roll-preview.js. No registry seat, no saved state, no production provider of its own. The three older hardwired declarations are unchanged.

PART I Feature 4.5.16 - Heart of Vengeance (A06): saves one rival Clan or faction (open list; Clans, Imperial families and the Brotherhood of Shinsei suggested), 5 XP or 4 for a Spider character, and registers the first production provider with Feature 4.5.15's declaration registry: an unticked 'Contested against <faction> - apply +1k1' on Skill, Trait, Ring and manual rolls only, never saved, +1k1 at most once per roll. Declared dependency on 4.5.15 (guarded; without it the rival is still recorded and priced). Ordered after 209.927 so the registry exists when it registers.

PART I Feature 4.57 - Unlucky (D05), the last of the audit's 23 missing configuration handlers and the only one needing dice-engine work. Installed through Phase 4.5.2's D45.install() seam, which Feature 4.56 could NOT use: D45.refresh() requires a d45 entry to sit in #disadvList, and Unlucky does. 2 XP per rank with one use per rank per session (rank 5 = 10 XP and 5/5 uses, not 10/10). The GM-invoke button on every roll result rerolls the SAVED pool via Phase 4.5's own advConfigLuckRerollResult and keeps the second result in all cases, even when better; because that helper never re-enters the action, no spell slot, Void point, Willpower gate or limited resource can be charged twice. Ordered after 209.92 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.56's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.58 - Dependant (D02) and Wrath of the Kami (D07), two more of the audit's missing configuration handlers and the first pair needing no dice-engine work. Both install through Phase 4.5.2's D45.install() seam. Dependant takes the player/GM-agreed point value as a free positive integer and prices the award at exactly that, with optional who-depends-on-you and arrangement fields on the ROW rather than in the modal, because D45.readStep() has no optional step; the catalogue's 'roughly 2-6' stays guidance and never becomes a ladder. Wrath of the Kami stores one element from the five the sheet's own spell library actually carries (Universal excluded) and awards 3, or 4 for a Shugenja, showing an incoming-spell Free Raise reminder for the player to communicate - it registers no pre-roll modifier because the Free Raise belongs to the other caster. Reuses D45's existing rankPick and elementPick type strings rather than adding one, because 4.5.2's harness pins configTypes to an exact array. Ordered after 209.93 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.57's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.59 - Doubt (D03), and the FIRST build of the approved TN-reporting convention: a rule's TN +N is represented as -N to the reported total, for Ring/Trait/Skill/spell/attack rolls only and NEVER for damage. D04's Benten and Fukurokujin branches reuse this machinery, so it is built here on the simplest consumer. Picks one current School Skill from D45's own state().schoolSkills, awards a fixed 4, and contributes a -5 totalDelta on Skill rolls and weapon attacks made with that Skill. Filters on roll KIND first and skill name second, because a damage context carries the same skillName and would otherwise be penalised. Takes NO new registry seat: it re-registers Phase 4.5's own adv-config contributor, which registerPreRollModifier replaces rather than appends, keeping Phase 1.5's baseline at seven. A stale Skill after a School change keeps its award and stops applying, rather than silently repricing a saved character. Ordered after 209.94 so its rebindings wrap Feature 4.58's. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.5.10 - Cursed by the Realm (D01), ten Spirit Realm branches behind one catalogue row. Installs through Phase 4.5.2's D45.install() seam and awards 4, or 5 for a Shugenja. Takes NO registry seat and re-registers nothing: its modifiers are reached through D45.modules, which D45.modifiers() consults generically from the single existing adv-config contributor - which also means ROLL_KINDS.DAMAGE never reaches this fragment at all, because D45.modifiers() returns early for it. Chikushudo applies -1k1 to Animal Handling; Meido scopes -1k0 on the roll's own traitName rather than a hand-written skill list; Tengoku is the second consumer of the TN-reporting convention; Maigo no Musha declares per roll through four guarded hooks in Phase 3's preview and is never left armed; Toshigoku offers a standalone Willpower check built on the trunk's own tnConfig; Yomi flags ancestral entries without deleting any. Jigoku's resistance roll is DEFERRED on the project owner's decision - the applicable roll is stated nowhere in the sheet and inventing it would be inventing rules content. Adds the realmPick configTypes string, with 4.5.2's exact-array assertion made conditional the way Phase 1.5's registry check already is. Ordered after 209.95 so its install runs against the fully-extended D45. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.5.11 - Seven Fortunes' Curse (D04a), five of the seven Fortune branches behind one catalogue row. Installs through Phase 4.5.2's D45.install() seam and awards 3, or 6 for Hotei, which is the sourcebook's own exception. Takes NO registry seat and re-registers nothing: like Feature 4.5.10 its modifiers are reached through D45.modules, so ROLL_KINDS.DAMAGE never reaches this fragment at all. Benten (Etiquette TN +10) and Fukurokujin (Lore TN +5, matched as a prefix so specializations are included) are the third and fourth consumers of the TN-reporting convention; Daikoku applies -1k1 to Commerce and REMINDS about its starting-koku reduction rather than debiting money, because the sheet's only koku field holds current money and the School's starting koku exists solely as free text; Ebisu (-1k1) and Jurojin (-2k0) declare per roll through four guarded hooks in Phase 3's preview, handling a LIST so both can be offered on one roll, and are never left armed. Ebisu scopes on D45.socialSkills - Feature 4.5.2's own authoritative Social Skill list - rather than declaring a second one. Bishamon and Hotei are DEFERRED to D04b by explicit scoping decision but remain pickable and correctly priced, carrying an honest row note, which is Jigoku's shape from Feature 4.5.10. Installs under BOTH apostrophe spellings of its name, because this is the first D45 entry whose catalogue name carries a curly apostrophe and D45's own norm() does not fold them. Adds the fortunePick configTypes string, with the other phases' exact-array assertions made conditional the way Feature 4.5.10 already made them. Ordered after 209.96 so its install runs against the fully-extended D45. New in this point release.

PART I Feature 4.5.12 - Seven Fortunes' Curse: Bishamon (D04b), D04's sixth branch and the first 4.5.x entry that CANNOT use the pre-roll modifier pipeline. Measured: rollWeaponDamage() never calls applyPreRollModifiers() - it rolls getWeaponDamageDice()'s numbers directly and consults the pipeline only afterwards to decorate the modal - so a modifier would print a penalty the dice never took. It reduces the STRENGTH CONTRIBUTION inside the damage maths instead, through two purely additive guarded blocks in 100-dice-engine.js, which is what the audit asks for in rules terms as well. Keys on the traitName that function already reports, so the three branches the audit wants checked separately fall out: Bow Strength is reduced inside its own min() (a bow whose rating already binds loses nothing), ordinary Strength covers melee, thrown and unarmed, Perception weapons and flat-DR weapons are untouched. Effective Strength floors at 1 - a measured decision from the Strength input's own minimum of 1, since an effective 0 makes unarmed roll 0k1 which rollWeaponDamage() refuses outright. Takes NO registry seat (the pipeline is not involved) and needs NO edit to 209.97: it retunes that phase's own mutable Bishamon spec and wraps its decorateRow, keeping the previous binding. Hotei stays deferred. Ordered after 209.97 so the spec it retunes is fully built. Kill-switch DISADV_BISHAMON_ENABLED. New in this point release.

BUGFIX - Mastery Rank Labelling. The weapon damage breakdown named the rank the CHARACTER holds as the rank that GRANTED a mastery effect: a Kenjutsu Rank 8 character read 'Kenjutsu Rank 8 mastery +1k0', though Kenjutsu's masteries are at Ranks 3 and 7 and Rank 8 grants nothing. Reported from a real device on 17 September 2026 during Feature 4.5.12's pass. The arithmetic was correct throughout; only the attribution was wrong. Not a string change: getDamageBonus() and getReductionModifier() SUM every unlocked threshold and getExplosionThreshold() returns only the lowest unlocked value, none of them recording which threshold contributed - so the granting rank is re-derived here from the skill's own threshold KEYS, which getStructuredMastery() already returns whole for Phase 3's (Part G) debug button. Rewrites the three lines IN PLACE through two purely additive guarded blocks in 100-dice-engine.js, leaving any line it does not recognise (the masteryDamageExempt notice, which carries no rank) untouched. Accumulating tables name every contributing threshold; explosion thresholds SUPERSEDE rather than accumulate, so only the one supplying the value in force is named. On the legacy-fallback path the printed numbers did not come from the structured table, so no rank is claimed at all. Ordered last among the sheet fragments so it can see every definition it reads. Kill-switch MASTERY_RANK_LABEL_FIX_ENABLED. New in this bugfix.

BUGFIX - Negative Roll Modifier Display. A negative flat total modifier was printed with a hardcoded '+' in front of it: the roll modal read 'Keeping 3 of 5 (suggested 3) + -40 bonus' on a wounded character with no Disadvantage configured. Pre-existing since Wound Penalties (Part C, Feature 3) first produced a negative totalDelta, and confirmed as such by Feature 4.5.9 rather than being that phase's. result.bonus sums TWO unlike things - the Ten Dice Rule's conversion bonus (always >= 0) and the pipeline's totalDelta (wounds, firing into melee, a required Raise) - so the number can be net negative and the word in front of it has to follow. MEASURED: three sites format it with a hardcoded '+' and TWO are visible - the keep-note (reported) and the NOTATION line, which read '12k4 -> 10k5 +-40' and was not reported. Both are corrected here through guarded blocks in 100-dice-engine.js that keep the trunk's own expression as the fallback. The third site is left alone deliberately: it can only malform when totalDelta is non-zero, which is exactly when attachRollModifierBreakdown() hides it, and correcting only its sign would leave it calling a wound penalty a Ten Dice Rule bonus. formatRollNotation() has the same shape but reads applyTenDiceRule() directly, whose bonus is built from non-negative counts and cannot go negative - measured, not assumed. Positive values are unchanged byte for byte. Ordered last among the sheet fragments so it can see every definition it reads. Kill-switch NEGATIVE_ROLL_MOD_DISPLAY_FIX_ENABLED. New in this bugfix.
